topics.Game Theory & Networks: Economic theory of strategic interaction: Nash equilibrium, repeated and dynamic games, bargaining, cooperative games, network formation and network games.
topics.Mechanism & Market Design: Economic theory of mechanism design, incentive compatibility, auctions, matching, allocation rules, and market design.
topics.Information & Contracts: Economic theory of asymmetric information, information design, Bayesian persuasion, signaling, screening, principal-agent models and contract theory.
topics.Decision & Social Choice: Economic theory of preferences, choice axioms, decisions under uncertainty, expected utility, voting, social choice, aggregation and welfare.
topics.Equilibrium & Mathematical Economics: Microeconomic theory foundations of competitive general equilibrium, production and exchange economies, equilibrium existence and uniqueness, welfare theorems and mathematical foundations of preferences.
topics.Industrial Organization Theory: Microeconomic theory of oligopoly, Cournot and Bertrand competition, monopoly pricing, market entry, search, platforms and strategic firm behavior.

negative_prototypes: An empirical economics paper estimating causal effects using regression, difference in differences, instrumental variables, survey data or field experiments.
A quantitative macroeconomics or finance paper calibrated to data to forecast returns, estimate risk or measure policy effects.
An engineering or computer science application optimizing wireless communications, energy systems, machine learning algorithms, security or vehicle routing.
A legal, medical, management or historical paper reviewing policy, institutional practice or philosophical arguments.
notes: Discovery of microeconomic-theory candidates only. Semantic embedding retrieval and text checks never authorize publication. A separate content-fingerprint approval gate in curation.json controls the public page, JSON and RSS. Scores are cosine similarities, not quality judgments. Explicit deposited JEL codes support retrieval only; no official SSRN category feed is claimed.

publication.scope: Microeconomic theory: game theory and networks; mechanism and market design; information and contracts; decision and social choice; general equilibrium foundations; theoretical industrial organization.
publication.policy: Daily discovery produces candidates, not automatic public recommendations. Publication requires a content-specific approval matching the current title, authors and abstract fingerprint. There is no daily publication quota.
publication.limits: Codex-assisted scope and contribution screening, not peer review, proof verification, a ranking, or a guarantee of novelty or quality. Author reputation and institutional affiliation are not admission rules. Papers not selected are not judged to be poor research.
outside_scope: Empirical or calibrated macroeconomics, growth and asset-pricing exercises without a primary microeconomic-theory contribution
Engineering, transport and operational optimization whose principal contribution is an application or numerical procedure
Management frameworks, policy commentary and conceptual essays without a substantive microeconomic-theory contribution
publication.boundary_note: Applications to macroeconomics, finance, public policy or technology do not disqualify a paper whose main contribution is to microeconomic-theory foundations.

10.2139/ssrn.7615221.reason: A welfare-weighted sufficient statistic for environmental valuation may be substantive welfare theory, not merely an application. Need the second-best fiscal derivation and identification assumptions to assess the general contribution; the primary source was unavailable.

10.2139/ssrn.7615220.reason: Comparative statics of Leontief-Fisher allocations are in scope. Need the regularity assumptions for the gainers' halfspace and equilibrium-path results, and their relation to the arithmetic claims; the primary SSRN page could not be retrieved.

10.2139/ssrn.7614238.reason: Documents nonrandom patent-examiner assignments using four million applications and a supporting investment model. The independent contribution is empirical identification of manipulation, not a new allocation mechanism or general strategic theorem.

10.2139/ssrn.7612338.reason: Optimizes a scenario-specific emissions-abatement budget and benchmarks reinforcement learning against dynamic programming. Exact optimization and simulated climate costs alone do not constitute microeconomic theory.

10.2139/ssrn.7615485.reason: The lattice and multiplicity results for insurance-price generalized Nash equilibria may qualify as game theory. Need the payoff monotonicity and feasible-set assumptions to assess the equilibrium results independently of the approximation algorithm; the primary paper was unavailable.

10.2139/ssrn.7614139.reason: Optimizes an exogenously specified actuarial welfare-and-smoothness objective over retirement-age schedules. The stated contribution is an applied pension scheduling toolkit, without strategic behavior or a new welfare/choice foundation.

10.2139/ssrn.7544244.reason: Regularizes inverse price-impact statistics using tick-size rounding and validates the metric on cryptocurrency data. This is market-measurement methodology, not strategic microstructure or equilibrium theory.

10.2139/ssrn.7539620.reason: Compares emissions-permit allocation and macroprudential policies in an environmental DSGE model with financial frictions. The abstract offers quantitative transition-risk policy analysis rather than equilibrium or preference foundations.

10.2139/ssrn.7540179.reason: Combines descriptive macro-finance data, corporate leverage arithmetic and arguments about wealth compounding. It does not provide a specified microeconomic model with a substantive analytical result.

10.2139/ssrn.7543618.reason: Estimates schooling responses to Chinese sectoral reallocation and motivates them with a simple labor-demand model. The main contribution is an empirical development-labor mechanism, not an independent general theory result.

10.2139/ssrn.7543686.reason: Formalizes an agent-payment software gate, admission tokens and concurrent spending invariants. Its proofs concern protocol correctness, not economic incentive compatibility, preferences or allocation efficiency.

10.2139/ssrn.7543259.reason: Develops censored-likelihood estimation and regret bounds for learning markdown prices in a depleting customer pool. Its principal contribution is a revenue-management learning algorithm, not strategic demand or general pricing-equilibrium theory.

10.2139/ssrn.7543098.reason: Estimates heterogeneous domestic quality responses to Indian FDI liberalization. The proposed competition mechanism is not accompanied by a substantive independent analytical theory result in the abstract.

10.2139/ssrn.7543001.reason: Empirically compares volatility-surface calibration, arbitrage interpolation and derivative prices. It is quantitative derivative-model validation, not economic allocation or preference foundations.

10.2139/ssrn.7538920.reason: Benchmarks Q-learning against dynamic programming in an existing constrained life-cycle consumption model. Its results concern computational performance and calibrated welfare losses, not a new theory of preferences or equilibrium.

10.2139/ssrn.7542940.reason: Optimal indemnity shapes under several risk criteria may be substantive insurance-contract theory. Need the admissible contract class, sponsor objective and any incentive constraints to assess the design and moral-hazard claims before selection.
